newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma's Suu Kyi protests confinement at home.
newsitem.headline: Burma's Suu Kyi protests confinement at home.

text.p: Burmese opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi on Wednesday protested against her confinement at home by the military government and labelled it an illegal move.
"We will make it known to the authorities that we protest this illegal confinement. Everytime there is a demonstration some people always take it as their job to put up roadblocks," she told Reuters.

Suu Kyi was restricted to her home indefinitely by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) following demonstrations by students of the Yangon Institute of Technology in Rangoon on Monday and early Tuesday.
She believed the confinement was imposed because the student protests made the government feel the situation was volatile.
"But the volatile situation has nothing to do with me or the National League for Democracy (NLD)," she said.
Suu Kyi denied any link between the student protests and the NLD but noted that there was a moral tie between the students' cause and that of her NLD party as both sought justice and human rights.
